decisions.quote: The research presented in this study replicates and extends the QSport-10 scale proposed by Rial, Varela, Rial and Real in their 2010 study, by incorporating the Programme dimension into the original measurement of service quality in Physical Activity and Sports Centres (PSCs). The objective of this research is to examine the dimensionality of the QSport-10 scale and extend it to capture the additional Programme service quality dimension. Study results confirmed the dimensionality of the service quality measurement offered by the QSport-10 scale and presented strong empirical support for the existence of Programme, Installations and Staff dimensions.

decisions.quote:
In the seventh installment of
Data Replicada
, we report our attempt to replicate a recently published
Journal of Consumer Research
(JCR) article entitled, “Product Entitativity: How the Presence of Product Replicates Increases Perceived and Actual Product Efficacy” (

In this paper, the authors propose that “presenting multiple product replicates as a group (vs. presenting a single item) increases product efficacy perceptions because it leads consumers to perceive products as more homogenous and unified around a shared goal” (abstract).
This JCR paper contains five studies. We chose to replicate Study 1 (N = 87) because it was the only study run on MTurk.

decisions.quote: However, the construct validity of this type of IAT has been called into question by recent findings showing that the IAT score implying in-group preference is rather driven by the salience asymmetry within each categorical dyad of the procedure than by evaluative associations between concepts (Rothermund & Wentura, 2001, 2004). In order to assess the validity of an IAT purported to measure French people’s prejudice toward North Africans in France, we conducted two studies that were designed to test the influence of salience asymmetry on an individual’s IAT score.

corrected_value.title: Improving arithmetic performance with number sense training: An investigation of underlying mechanism

decisions.location: Introduction (line 6); see also Methods (lines 16-24, Table 1 lines 94-100), Results (lines 43, 47-55), Discussion (lines 59-66), and References (line 165)
decisions.quote: Unexpectedly, we failed to replicate the approximate arithmetic training effect in Experiments 1 and 2. Consequently, we attempted more precise replications of Park & Brannon, 2013, 2014 in Experiment 3 (approximate arithmetic training compared to numeral ordering training) and a preregistered replication in Experiment 4 (approximate arithmetic training compared to approximate number comparison training). Finally, to increase the power for detecting any transfer effect we analyzed the data from Experiments 1-4 combined with the original data from the Park and Brannon experiments. Over four experiments and 318 participants we found no support for the original claim that training adults on the approximate arithmetic task benefits symbolic arithmetic fluency.
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent (never-adjudicated work). Across four experiments (N = 318), the authors empirically retest the transfer effect of non-symbolic approximate arithmetic training on symbolic arithmetic fluency reported in both Park & Brannon (2013) and Park & Brannon (2014). In particular, Experiment 3 tests approximate arithmetic vs. numeral symbol ordering (present in both 2013 Exp 2 and 2014 Exp 1) and Experiment 4 is a preregistered replication of approximate arithmetic vs. approximate number comparison, a control condition introduced and tested specifically in Park & Brannon (2014) Experiment 1 (Methods line 22; Table 1 lines 94-100). The authors also re-analyze the original Park & Brannon (2014) Experiment 1 data and compare effect sizes directly against it (Results lines 47-55). Shipped row 2491 (10.1177/0956797613482944) covers only the 2013 Psychological Science paper (sibling target_index 0); Park & Brannon (2014) in Cognition (10.1016/j.cognition.2014.06.011) reports a separate independent experiment (N = 71, four conditions) and is genuinely absent from all shipped rows.

decisions.location: Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References (line 1)
decisions.quote: Despite the theoretical and practical importance of TIME, there has not yet been a replication of the combined behavioural results of Clouter et al. (2017) and Wang et al. (2018) outside the original research group. Of particular importance for interpretation of memory enhancement effects is a replication in which all relevant control conditions (asynchronous theta, no-flicker, and synchronous non-theta) are combined in a single experiment. This is the aim of the present experiment.
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent (never-adjudicated work). This Stage 2 Registered Report collects new data (N = 32) to empirically retest the combined behavioural theta-induced memory effect (TIME) reported by both Clouter et al. (2017) and Wang et al. (2018). The study powers its sample size on the smallest effect size across Clouter et al. (2017) and Wang et al. (2018), adapts experimental code provided by D. Wang, compares synchronous vs. asynchronous theta recognition accuracy (41.4%) directly against the 46.4% and 42.8% reported by Clouter et al. (2017) and Wang et al. (2018), and explicitly concludes in the Discussion that it failed to replicate the TIME reported by both Clouter et al. (2017) and Wang et al. (2018). Shipped row 1057 (10.1016/j.cub.2017.09.001) represents only Clouter et al. (2017) (sibling target_index 0). Wang et al. (2018) in The Journal of Neuroscience (38(28): 6299-6309, doi: 10.1523/JNEUROSCI.0349-18.2018) reports a separate experiment with new EEG/behavioural data and is genuinely absent from all shipped rows.
